overview: Two complementary processes that break down food, one using physical force and the other using enzymes to break chemical bonds.
genZNote: Mechanical digestion: physically ripping food into smaller pieces. Chemical digestion: enzymes breaking the actual molecular bonds.

aspects.label: Method
aspects.valueA: Physical breakdown of food into smaller pieces (chewing, churning) without changing its chemical structure.
aspects.valueB: Enzymatic breakdown of large food molecules into simpler chemical units.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Chewing (mastication) in the mouth, churning in the stomach.
aspects.valueB: Amylase breaking down starch into maltose.

aspects.label: Purpose
aspects.valueA: Increases surface area for enzymes to act on more efficiently.
aspects.valueB: Actually converts complex molecules into simpler, absorbable units.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Mechanical digestion doesn't change food chemically at all — its entire purpose is to increase surface area so chemical digestion can work faster and more completely.
overlay.memoryTrick: Mechanical = breaking it into smaller pieces. Chemical = breaking the actual bonds.
overlay.commonMisconception: Chewing alone does not digest starch — chemical digestion (starting with salivary amylase) is what actually begins breaking it down, even though it starts in the same place (the mouth).
